newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end up after wide price swings.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end up after wide price swings.

text.p: CME pork belly futures finished a wild session marked by wide price swings mostly higher, buoyed by fund and mixed short covering after tumbling from early limit gains, traders said. Hog futures finished mixed with nearbys weaker.

Frozen pork belly contracts finished 0.875 cent per lb higher to 0.500 lower with July up most at 91.600 cents after trading in a 3.425- cent range and posting a limit gain of 3.000 cents early. Hog futures finished 0.250 cent a lb lower to 0.325 higher with June off most at 83.650 cents.

Profit taking developed in bellies when futures jumped to limit gains early. Talk that cash belly prices were slipping, especially with USDA reporting lackluster cash dealings and nominal prices, weighed on futures after early strength.

But renewed fund buying firmed bellies late. Expectations that the CME out of town storage report would be bullish reinforced gains stemming from recent light hog slaughter levels and subsequent tighter belly supplies.

"What helped the cash belly market (recently) is the light supply (of hogs). If we had the same amount of hogs as came in a year ago we would have had some pretty good storage the last couple of weeks," said Rick Tokheim of Investment Research Co.
USDA estimated U.S. hog slaughter through Tuesday at 622,000 head, below 625,000 in the same period a week ago and well below 697,000 a year ago.

After the close, the CME reported net out-movement from CME-approved warehouses outside Chicago last week of 1.205 million lbs versus analysts' estimates ranging from in-movement of 200,000 lbs to out-movement of 200,000 lbs. The figure also compared with 409,000 lb-out-movement last week and an in-movement of 257,000 lbs last year.
"We had a lighter kill that week, but it still implies a pretty strong usage level - it's probably some export business," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.
Skold said belly futures will likely open sharply higher Wednesday following the report.

Prudential Securities and Smith Barney bought July before Prudential turned sellers along with LFG at the limit up, traders said. LIT division/First Options and mixed short covering lifted May before Refco sold. Smith Barney, R.J. O'Brien and Spike Trading bought July late, pit sources said.

Hog futures followed the lead of pork bellies much of the day but ended mostly weaker on expectations of weak cash hog markets Wednesday. Rain is forecast for much of the Midwest which likely will take farmers from fieldwork and allow more time to market hogs.
Futures were supported early by higher cash hog prices Tuesday.

Rand Financials sold June and July late while buying August. ABN Chicogo Corp and Spike Trading bought July early. In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought October 82 calls early and Cargill Investor Services bought June 90 calls late, pit sources said.
